guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our modest preference for Maryland starts with an offense that has shown credible early balance. Malik Washington has completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards without an interception, while Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. both topped 100 receiving yards at UConn. We are not treating two games as proof, but that production gives us more confidence that Maryland can sustain offense through the air rather than depend on short fields or turnovers.

We also see support on the other side of the ball. Maryland allowed 154 total yards and seven points per game through its first two contests while recording 10 sacks. That pressure is relevant against a UCLA passing offense our numbers rate poorly, but the matchup is not uniformly favorable for Maryland.

For us, that last point is why this remains a pass. Our longer-run numbers see UCLA's rushing offense as a legitimate challenge for Maryland's defense, creating enough uncertainty to offset the encouraging early results. We differ slightly from the market, but not by enough to make the available price worthwhile.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching UCLA's rushing offense against Maryland's rush defense. Maryland allowed only 38.5 rushing yards per game through two games, but our broader efficiency numbers are much less flattering to that unit and considerably more favorable to UCLA on the ground. The question is whether Maryland's early run prevention reflects something sustainable or whether UCLA can keep its offense out of the difficult passing situations in which Maryland's pass rush becomes most influential.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, 2026.
Maryland produced 475 total yards, 27 first downs and no turnovers against UConn, including 350 passing yards and 125 rushing yards.
Maryland held UConn to 223 total yards, 67 rushing yards, 156 passing yards and 12 first downs while recording five sacks.
Maryland had second-quarter scoring drives of 92 and 91 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: Maryland's most recent game against UCLA was a road loss on Oct. 18, 2025, decided by between one and nine points.
Malik Washington completed 23 of 48 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception at UCLA in 2025; he also rushed six times for 67 yards.
DeJuan Williams had 14 carries for 47 yards and seven receptions for 86 yards at UCLA in 2025.
Cornerback Jamare Glasker recorded an interception and three tackles at UCLA in 2025.
Linebacker Sidney Stewart recorded three tackles, including a five-yard sack, at UCLA in 2025.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Malik Washington is 53-of-72 for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions through Maryland's first two games of 2026.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns at UConn, including a Maryland-record 18 consecutive completions.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and completed 273 passes for 2,963 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Transfer backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed four of five passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's starting offensive line against UConn was left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright; the unit blocked for 475 total yards.
Amory Hills replaced Tellek Lockette as the starting left guard between the Hampton opener and the UConn game.
Rahtrel Perry entered the Virginia Tech week with 39 consecutive career starts, the most among Maryland offensive players.

Transfer receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. each exceeded 100 receiving yards at UConn: Gladding had eight catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, and Durr had 10 catches for 106 yards and a touchdown.

Maryland added 17 transfers for 2026, including receivers Gladding, Durr and Ejani Shakir; running back Harry Dalton III; tight end Preston Howard; offensive lineman Tellek Lockette; and quarterbacks Cardell Williams and Jack Capaldi.
Harry Dalton III had career highs of 48 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns at UConn, while Iverson Howard rushed 14 times for 55 yards and one touchdown.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's starting defense against UConn included defensive linemen Lavon Johnson and Eyan Thomas, edge defenders Nahsir Taylor and Sidney Stewart, linebackers Trey Reddick and Daniel Wingate, cornerbacks Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson and Jordan Scruggs, and safeties Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs.
Maryland added defensive-line transfers Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon and Jayvon Parker from Washington, plus defensive back Amari Jackson from Boston College.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn.

Randy Starks joined Maryland to coach the defensive line, and Kyle Schmitt took over the tight ends room.
